cues.en: In this chapter, we will have a look at why loops in bash.
They allow us to repeatedly execute block of code.
And this can be useful if we want to repeat a certain part of our script.
It works by first checking a condition, and as long as this condition is fulfilled, a code block is
executed over and over again until the initial condition is no longer fulfilled.
Let's say, for example, we want to read a text file line by line, and we do not know ahead how large
In that case, we can use a while loop to go through that file and print out each individual line or
work with each individual line and then decide what we want to do with that content.
We will have a look at exactly this example later here in this chapter.
Also, this allows us to write a script that triggers multiple downloads without us knowing before how
many downloads we want to do.
